scenarios.title: Repair LDAP client defaults after a directory move
scenarios.summary: Separate a directory URI, a search base and a search scope while repairing a client lookup.
scenarios.objective: Repair the virtual client defaults to use ldap://directory.cedar.test and the People branch (ou=People,dc=cedar,dc=test). Write a search returning every person in that subtree, including Remote, with uid and cn only. Exclude Archive. Verify both the changed directory and the disclosed default-setting checks; a -b override alone does not repair BASE.
steps: Repair the virtual configuration, run actual simulated searches and check the independent cases.
scenarios.explanation: URI chooses directory.cedar.test and BASE chooses ou=People,dc=cedar,dc=test. A subtree person filter includes both direct People users and the nested Remote user. uid/cn selects the required output fields. A one-command -b can diagnose the correct branch, but the independent configured-default checks still fail until BASE is repaired. A missing base, zero matches and an unavailable supplied URI are different outcomes.

Use the sample directory and inspect a failed case. A missing base is different from no matching entries.

Use new numeric OIDs below 1.3.6.1.4.1.32473.220; leave the supplied base definitions unchanged. trainingBadge: Required text value, exactly one per trainingPerson; declare a compatible text equality rule. trainingPoints: Optional Integer values with integer equality. Several distinct values must work; invalid formats and equal duplicates must fail. trainingPerson: Inherit person, including cn and sn. Allow uid and trainingPoints, plus inherited optional description; reject unlisted fields. Verify and preserve data: Accept every valid Add/replacement and reject invalid data without changing stored entries. Check all three sample sets.

scenarios.explanation: MUST makes the badge required; SINGLE-VALUE limits its value count. SUP person preserves required cn and sn fields, and MAY allows optional identifiers and points. Integer syntax rejects words and leading-zero encodings; integerMatch prevents duplicate equal point values. A rejected request must leave the actual stored entry unchanged. scenarios.title: Repair directory matching for a consumer
scenarios.summary: Connect declared text comparison rules to actual filter results across changing directory records.
scenarios.objective: Schema: Add one consumer schema with new OIDs below 1.3.6.1.4.1.32473.230; preserve the supplied base definitions and accessPerson inheritance from person. Allow uid, accessTeam and accessState. Team labels: accessTeam ignores letter case and insignificant spaces; distinct labels stay distinct. State codes: accessState preserves letter case, so active differs from Active; text equality still ignores insignificant spaces. Filter: Select entries having team Aster and state active. One matching team value is enough. Exclude other states, other teams and entries missing either criterion. Verification: All supplied rosters, verification after names and user IDs change and required comparison tests must pass. Resolve Undefined results; avoid hardcoding individual names.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the named comparison or selection failure. Repair one cause, run the selected sample, then check all samples again.
steps: Repair comparison rules and verify one filter against all supplied records.
scenarios.explanation: caseIgnoreMatch makes accessTeam compare Aster and ASTER as the same label; caseExactMatch keeps active different from Active in accessState. Both supported text rules ignore insignificant spaces. An AND filter requires a matching team value and the exact active state. Presence alone, OR, a hardcoded person or a filter with an unknown field does not satisfy the full set of rosters and rule checks. Only True selects an entry; NOT leaves Undefined unresolved.
hints: Separate the attribute value format, its comparison rule and the filter logic. A changed filter alone may not repair the required schema behavior.
Team labels and state codes have different requirements for letter case. A filter must require both the matching team and active state.
Use the sample data to distinguish a missing field from an unknown descriptor. Check changed rosters instead of filtering by person names.
scenarios.simplifications: Checked2026-11-09: LPIC-2v4.5/210.3/210.4 and RFC4511/4512/4515/4517/4518. Bounded printable-ASCII schema/entry/filter activity; all supplied entries are evaluated without a search base, scope, projection, ACL or protocol operation. Equality/presence/AND/OR/NOT only; numeric attribute aliases, options, substring/ordering/extensible filters and Unicode are explicitly unsupported. No host command/files, process, server or network; no actual OpenLDAP comparison or full-objective claim. Three rosters are behavioral cases, not extra labs.
